_readme: Phase F2 — recorded confidence-calibration baseline.
The F2 acceptance criterion is: 'on a held-out history, the calibration
curve (predicted vs. actual resolution) is measurably closer to the
diagonal after recalibration than before'. This file records that
measurement and the margin asserted in CI.
The fixture models the failure mode a real deployment has: an
OVERCONFIDENT platform. Stated confidence rises with the strength of the
evidence, but at every level the actual resolution rate is well below the
number stated — a '0.9' resolves 55% of the time. That is the shape
AEAM's additive confidence produces (independent components each adding
a little, with nothing checking the total against reality), and it is why
confidence could not be used to set an automation threshold before F2.
ECE is the sample-weighted mean distance between each bucket's stated
confidence and its observed rate — literally the distance of the
reliability curve from the diagonal. Brier accompanies it because ECE
alone can be gamed by a model that predicts the base rate for everything
(perfectly calibrated, entirely uninformative); Brier punishes exactly
that, so requiring BOTH to improve rules the degenerate solution out.
Every number below is measured on the HELD-OUT split, which the isotonic
fit never saw. Measuring on training data would report a near-zero ECE
for any mapping and prove nothing.

fixture.note: Deterministic: the same commit always produces the same score, so a regression is unambiguous.

required_margins._note: Asserted by test_phase_f2_learning.py. Set below the measured values so ordinary variation does not fail the build, but high enough that a broken fit does.
